statement: Let M = 1000000007. Whenever the function returns a result r, r is the remainder modulo M of the number of special permutations of nums: that is, the number of sequences p of length n such that (a) p is a permutation of nums (each value of nums occurs in p exactly once), and (b) for every i with 0 <= i < n-1, either p[i] divides p[i+1] or p[i+1] divides p[i]. Equivalently, 0 <= r < M and r is congruent modulo M to that exact count T.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers; n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 14; every nums[i] is positive and all entries are distinct (hence 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9 under the problem constraints).

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, overflow, or go out of bounds.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers; n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 14; every nums[i] is positive and all entries are distinct.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= n!, where n! = 1*2*...*n.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers; n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 14; every nums[i] is positive and all entries are distinct.

statement: For every valid nums with len(nums) = 2, whenever the function returns a result r: if nums[0] divides nums[1] or nums[1] divides nums[0], then r = 2; otherwise r = 0.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers; n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 14; every nums[i] is positive and all entries are distinct.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if for every pair of indices i,j with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= j < n, and i != j, either nums[i] divides nums[j] or nums[j] divides nums[i], then r = (n! mod 1000000007).
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers; n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 14; every nums[i] is positive and all entries are distinct.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if for every pair of distinct indices i,j with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= j < n, and i != j, neither nums[i] divides nums[j] nor nums[j] divides nums[i], then r = 0.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers; n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 14; every nums[i] is positive and all entries are distinct.

statement: For every valid nums and every slice q of length n that is a permutation of nums (for every integer v, v occurs in q exactly as many times as in nums), if the call special_perm(nums) returns r and the call special_perm(q) returns r', then r = r'.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers; n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 14; every nums[i] is positive and all entries are distinct.

statement: For every valid nums and every positive integer c such that c*nums[i] <= 10^9 for every i with 0 <= i < n, let q be the slice with q[i] = c*nums[i]. If special_perm(nums) returns r and special_perm(q) returns r', then r = r'.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers; n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 14; every nums[i] is positive and all entries are distinct.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if r > 0 then there exists at least one special permutation of nums.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers; n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 14; every nums[i] is positive and all entries are distinct.

statement: For every valid nums with 2 <= len(nums) <= 12, whenever the function returns a result r, r is an even integer.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers; n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 14; every nums[i] is positive and all entries are distinct.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if there exist distinct indices i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n such that neither nums[i] divides nums[j] nor nums[j] divides nums[i], then, writing T for the exact number of special permutations of nums and n! = 1*2*...*n, there is a nonnegative integer q with T = q*1000000007 + r and T <= n! - 2*(n-1)!.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers; n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 14; every nums[i] is positive and all entries are distinct.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, let T be the exact number of special permutations of nums. Then there exists a nonnegative integer q such that T = q*1000000007 + r and T is even.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers; n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 14; every nums[i] is positive and all entries are distinct.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers; n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 14; every nums[i] is a positive integer with 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9, and all entries are distinct; there exists an index i with 0 <= i < n such that for every j with 0 <= j < n and j != i, neither nums[i] divides nums[j] nor nums[j] divides nums[i].

statement: Let T be the exact number of special permutations of nums. Whenever the function returns a result r, T = n! - 2*(n-1)! and consequently r = (n! - 2*(n-1)!) mod 1000000007.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers; n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 14; every nums[i] is a positive integer with 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9, and all entries are distinct; there is a unique unordered pair of distinct indices {i, j} such that neither nums[i] divides nums[j] nor nums[j] divides nums[i], and every other unordered pair of distinct indices is comparable by divisibility.
